minutes.headline: Planning Board heard residents on the water supply zoning article, agreed to amend it to address Zone One, and recommended all five articles.
minutes.summary: The special meeting was a public hearing on five zoning warrant articles for town meeting: water supply protection, solar canopies, the large-scale solar exclusion, driveways and entrances, and agricultural bylaw updates. Residents objected mainly to the water supply article's unreadable map and its silence on Zone One. The board agreed to propose clarifying amendments, closed the hearing and voted to recommend all the articles. The 274 Prospect Street decision was pushed to November 13.

attendees.role: vice chair / member (presiding for much of the hearing)

public_comment.topic: Initial public comment invited; none given, since attendees were there for the warrant article hearing.

The map referenced in the water supply article is illegible in the booklet, and it shows Zone One although the article is silent on it. She asked for a new map without Zone One and a statement that the planning board is not regulating Zone One.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, 50 Hemlock Drive, president of Hickory Hills Landowners Inc
public_comment.topic: Asked why only Zones 2 and 3 were addressed, why Zone One was not, and who owns the map. Said the Hickory Hills well sits on private property.
Supported Joan Peas's concerns about the Zone One map and asked for clarification.
Urged the board to state in the article that it has zero jurisdiction over Zone One, remove Zone One from the map, and make the article fully transparent.
Zoom chat question from Jack and Denny Brown (15 Winter Green Court) asking what the amendment would change in the water supply protection district.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, 50 Hemlock Drive, president of Hickory Hills Landowners Inc
public_comment.topic: Gave the history of the Hickory Hills landowners association and well. The well has been shut down for years because of manganese and iron.
Said the article is not clear or transparent, was voted down last year, and should not go to town meeting in its present condition. Wants the map and wording fixed.
Said the water district project showed no care for residents around Hickory Hills Lake and asked where citizens can go to be heard.
Questioned the motive, citing the water department's earlier interest in selling water to other towns.
Zoom chat from Jack and Denny Brown asking that the public see a list of specific changes.
Concerned that the 2021 map may already be visible on state GIS and affecting residents before the town votes on it.
Zoom chat question from Jack and Denny Brown asking whether swimming will be allowed.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing on the zoning warrant articles.
Recommend all five articles as presented, with the amendments discussed at the hearing.

budget_items.topic: Full-size printed map for town meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident asked for a large printed map at the entrance. The board member said the budget should allow it but he would verify first.
A board member said the water district does not cost taxpayers and is pay-as-you-use.

decisions.decision: The board agreed to propose two clarifying amendments to the water supply article: a statement that nothing in the section regulates Zone One, and a definition of Zone One, using Mr Harris's wording.
A board member will try to get a legible map to residents, digitally and at town meeting, and will raise the printing and communication problem with the town manager.

The board will propose Mr Harris's suggested amendment on solar canopy height: the planning board may grant a greater height by special permit for emergency and service vehicles. It will go in the town meeting slide deck.
The storm water permit decision for 274 Prospect Street was not voted tonight; it will go to the November 13 meeting after corrections. The chair must review the October 23 hearing before voting.
The chair proposed that, before the master plan arrives, the board shore up existing bylaws (signs, solar). Members voiced agreement.
Counsel's recommended amendment would be moved at the outset of town meeting. If it fails, the article should be withdrawn.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to recommend all five zoning articles for town meeting, with the amendments discussed at the hearing, and closed the public hearing.
The board agreed to propose two clarifying amendments to the water supply article: a statement that nothing in it regulates Zone One, and a definition of Zone One.
Residents objected that the water supply article's map is illegible and shows Zone One, which the article does not mention; a board member will try to get a legible map to residents.
The board will propose a solar canopy amendment letting it grant extra height by special permit for emergency and service vehicles.
The storm water permit decision for 274 Prospect Street was not voted and moves to the November 13 meeting after corrections.

why_it_matters: The water supply protection article, which residents said was voted down last year, goes to town meeting with added wording on Zone One, so residents near the Hickory Hills well will be asked to vote on the amended text.
The solar canopy, driveway and agricultural bylaw changes are zoning rules that residents will be asked to vote on at town meeting, and the board's recommendation is on the record for all five.
